purpose:
A single-user macOS dictation application that captures speech, recognizes it, optionally rewrites it under a user-selected mode, and inserts the result into the application the user was working in. Every speech and language operation runs on the user's Mac. There is no cloud fallback, no account, no subscription gate, and no artificial cap on recording length or usage; the limits are the hardware and the models the user installs.

In scope: recording controls, text delivery, recording display, built-in modes, custom modes, automatic mode selection, vocabulary, context, languages, input sources, meetings, history, models, and desktop behavior. Out of scope: cloud inference, account-based settings sync, paywalls, enterprise billing and authentication, and any Windows or iOS client.

The whole product is designed before implementation phases are cut, because several requirements constrain the persistence schema, the process model, and the ingest boundary in ways that are expensive to retrofit: re-recognizing old audio through a different speech model while keeping every derived artifact attributable, deleting a recording while a worker is producing a result for it, snapshotting mode settings so a later edit cannot change the meaning of a saved result, recovering a crash at any stage without duplicating delivered text, and bounding memory on a multi-hour import across two processes. Left to whichever implementation task hits them first, those force the schema and the job model into a shape that cannot express them.

This revision changes five load-bearing parts of the earlier design: results now hang off identified processing runs rather than a single per-recording transcript; captured audio is journaled in independently recoverable chunks rather than assumed recoverable from a truncated container; the ingest port carries timing and flow control; text insertion is defined in terms of caret and selection with named observable signals; and every feasibility experiment that could invalidate a boundary is scheduled before that boundary is frozen.

The historical feature inventories from the user's mcwhisper and super experiments are evidence about desired scope. Their generated plans and dependency choices do not bind this design.

## Layering rule

One rule governs dependency direction: `DictationCore` depends only on `DictationPorts`; adapters depend on `DictationPorts` and on system frameworks; nothing depends on an adapter except the composition root in the app shell. `DictationCore` contains no AppKit, no AVFoundation, no SQLite, and no network code, so the run state machine, mode resolution, vocabulary pipeline, prompt assembly, output validation, and scheduling policy can be exercised without a microphone, a model, or a window server.

## Package and target layout (D-002)

Swift Package Manager package `LocalDictation` with library targets:

- `DictationPorts`: protocols and value types shared by core and adapters (`AudioSource`, `AudioFrame`, `SpeechRecognizer`, `TextGenerator`, `Diarizer`, `TextInserter`, `FocusObserver`, `ContextProvider`, `ModelStore`, `RecordingStore`, `LeaseBroker`, `ShortcutRegistrar`, `MediaController`, `RuntimeCapabilityDescriptor`).
- `DictationCore`: run state machine, `RunManifest` assembly, mode resolution, vocabulary pipeline, prompt assembly, `ResourceScheduler` policy, delivery policy.
- `TextValidation`: transformation contracts, validator checks, and per-language validator packs (segmentation, interrogative detection, content-word extraction).
- `DictationStore`: SQLite schema, migrations, repositories, the audio chunk journal and sealer, tombstones, generations, and the lease broker.
- `AudioIngest`: `AVAudioEngine` microphone source, `ScreenCaptureKit` system-audio source, `AVAssetReader` seekable file source, converters to the canonical recognition format.
- `SpeechRuntimeWhisperCpp` and (conditionally, per D-020) `SpeechRuntimeWhisperKit`: `SpeechRecognizer` adapters.
- `LanguageRuntimeClient`: IPC client for the generation helper.
- `SystemIntegration`: accessibility insertion, pasteboard, `CGEventTap` shortcuts, media control, status item, permission probes.
- `DictationUI`: SwiftUI views, recording panel, settings, history browser.

Executable targets: `dictation-llm-helper` and `dictation-asr-helper` (the latter when the chosen speech runtime is a C or C++ library). The shipping `.app` is a thin Xcode target depending on the package, because entitlements, hardened runtime, privacy usage strings, and notarization are not expressible in `Package.swift`. `swift test` covers core, store, validation, and the pure parts of adapters; the Xcode scheme adds UI and integration tests.

## Process model (D-003, D-028)

Three kinds of process: the app, inference helpers, and a downloader that runs only on explicit user action. Inference runs in child helper processes, never behind a local HTTP server. A local endpoint would bind a port reachable by every process on the machine, would need its own authentication, and is the component most likely to acquire forwarding behavior through configuration the app does not own; RESEARCH raises exactly this for llama.cpp's server tooling. Helpers receive model paths and audio windows over an inherited socket pair with a length-prefixed protocol and contain no socket-creation code.

The network claim is scoped to what the design can enforce. Build checks assert that helper targets and their SPM dependency closure import no networking modules and that the linked binaries reference no socket or CFNetwork symbols, and an integration test runs a complete session with the network denied. Those checks cannot prove that a system framework or dynamically loaded code performs no request, so the product states the guarantee as "the inference path contains and exercises no network code, verified by build checks and a network-denied session test" until gate F2 establishes an operating-system-level restriction, at which point the claim strengthens. Crash isolation and residency accounting hold independent of that outcome.

## Processing runs (D-029)

A recording owns audio artifacts. Every piece of derived text belongs to a `processing_run`, which pins the settings that produced it and names its entry stage. Runs come in four kinds: `dictation` (capture plus recognition through delivery), `import`, `reprocess_recognition` (re-runs recognition over stored audio), and `reprocess_text` (re-runs refining, rewriting, translation, or notes over a named earlier result). Only `dictation` runs may deliver text.

## The lifetime of a dictation run (D-006)

Component boundaries follow this sequence.

1. `idle`.
2. `arming` (budget 200 ms): resolve the effective mode from the automatic-selection rules; latch the delivery target (frontmost PID, bundle identifier, window number, focused `AXUIElement`, and whether that element supports settable selected text); sample context sources in parallel against the budget; assemble a `RunManifest` naming mode revision, speech model installation, language model installation, vocabulary revision, language setting, translation flag, and validator language pack; allocate a UUIDv7 recording id and run id; create the session directory; write and fsync manifest v0.
3. `capturing`: the audio source delivers timestamped native frames; a writer task appends them to the chunk journal (D-030) and feeds a provisional recognizer; the panel shows live text and an envelope.
4. `sealing`: stop the source, encode the journal into the library artifact, fsync, then commit the recording row, artifact row, and run row in one transaction. This is the first point at which the recording exists in History.
5. `recognizing`: a pass over the complete audio produces a recognition result with segment timings and per-segment average log-probability. The provisional stream is discarded rather than promoted; it was computed over partial context and is a different artifact.
6. `refining`: deterministic vocabulary replacement and optional filler removal produce a normalized result derived from that recognition result.
7. `rewriting` (only when the mode has a generation stage): prompt assembly, generation in the helper, contract validation.
8. `delivering`: exactly one attempt, guarded by a committed idempotency record.
9. Terminal: `complete`, `cancelled(stage)`, `failed(stage, reason)`, or `delivery_unresolved`.

Imports enter at step 3 with a seekable source and no delivery latch. Meetings enter at step 3 with two sources and continue to a notes run instead of delivery. Reprocessing enters at step 5 or step 6 with a manifest that names the parent result. One machine therefore serves every input source and every reprocessing path, which is why cancellation, recovery, and deletion have one definition each.

## Concurrency and ownership (D-004)

One `RunActor` per processing run owns that run's state, rows, and files; it is the only writer for them. Two runs on the same recording are serialized by the recording's lease broker. The audio callback thread never touches an actor, allocates, or locks; it writes frames and a 10 ms RMS and peak envelope into two lock-free rings.

A single `ResourceScheduler` actor admits model-bound work in three lanes. `capture` is never queued. `interactive` covers the provisional pass, the recognition and rewrite for the run the user is waiting on. `batch` covers imports, notes, and reprocessing. At most one speech job and one generation job hold a loaded model at a time. Whether an admitted batch job can be preempted depends on the runtime's measured capability descriptor rather than on assumption: descriptors record cancellation latency, whether a window boundary is a safe checkpoint, and whether resuming from a checkpoint reproduces the unpreempted transcript. A runtime that reports safe checkpoints yields at the next window; a runtime that does not is either cancelled and restarted from its last committed checkpoint or allowed to finish behind a bound the panel displays, chosen per runtime by descriptor. Until the F1 harness produces descriptors, the scheduler uses the cancel-and-restart policy, which is correct for both cases and slower for one.

## Component responsibilities

- `ModeResolver` (core): a pure function from (foreground app, URL when readable, explicit override, ordered rule list) to a mode revision.
- `VocabularyPipeline` (core): pure text-to-text with an explicit stage order and ICU-based segmentation.
- `PromptAssembler` (core): mode instructions, then context fenced with a per-run random delimiter and labeled as reference material, then the normalized transcript, then the task line restated.
- `ContractValidator` (`TextValidation`): checks generated text against the mode's structured transformation contract in the run's language, and decides between accept, retry once, and fall back to the normalized transcript.
- `DeliveryCoordinator` (core policy) plus `TextInserter` (adapter): focus and insertion policy separated from the insertion mechanism, so policy is testable without a window server.
- `RecordingStore` plus `LeaseBroker` (`DictationStore`): the only writers of History rows and library files, and the enforcement point for tombstones, generations, and leases for every writer including retention.

## Why this supports the whole scope as phases land

The run state machine, the manifest snapshot, the provenance graph, the recovery table, and the lease protocol all exist in phase 0 against fake adapters. Every later phase adds an adapter behind an existing port (an audio source, a speech runtime, a diarizer), a result kind (translation, notes), or a validator language pack. None of them changes how a run is recorded, cancelled, recovered, or deleted. The parts that are expensive to change late are built first and exercised against fakes, where cancel-at-every-stage and kill-at-every-boundary suites are cheap to run.

## Stores and ownership

`DictationStore` owns everything under `~/Library/Application Support/LocalDictation/`:

```
library.sqlite               metadata, runs, results, FTS index (WAL)
Recordings/<uuid>/manifest.json
Recordings/<uuid>/journal/<stream>/<seq>.pcm   durable capture chunks
Recordings/<uuid>/journal/<stream>/index.log   packet index for sealing
Recordings/<uuid>/audio/<stream>.caf           sealed library artifact
Recordings/<uuid>/source/<original filename>   imported original
Models/blobs/<sha256>/                          immutable verified installs
Models/.staging/<uuid>/                         in-flight downloads and imports
Scratch/<jobId>/                                worker temporaries
```

One writer connection in WAL mode; readers use separate connections. `RunActor` never writes SQLite directly; it calls repository methods that enforce tombstone, generation, and lease rules.

## Provenance graph (D-029)

- `recordings(id, created_at, source_kind, duration_ms, interrupted, deleted_at, generation, audio_state, display_run_id)`
- `audio_artifacts(id, recording_id, role, path, container, codec, sample_rate, channels, sealed_at, sha256, byte_length)` with `role` in {`microphone`, `system`, `imported_original`}
- `processing_runs(id, recording_id, recording_generation, kind, entry_stage, parent_result_id, manifest_json, state, started_at, ended_at, reason)`
- `results(id, run_id, recording_id, kind, derived_from_result_id, text, params_json, created_at)` with `kind` in {`recognition`, `normalized`, `rewritten`, `translation`, `notes`}
- `segments`, `speaker_clusters`, `speaker_identities`, `speaker_assignments`, `modes`, `mode_revisions`, `vocabulary_revisions`, `model_installations`, `active_models`, `leases`, `context_digests`, `delivery_attempts`, `jobs`

Every result names its immediate input. A recognition result has `derived_from_result_id = NULL` and is the root of its run's chain; normalized derives from recognition; rewritten derives from normalized; a translation derives from whichever result the user translated. A recording can hold several recognition results, one per recognition run, and each carries the speech model installation id that produced it. "The source transcript" is therefore a property of a run, not of a recording, and "which transcript did this rewrite use" is answered by a foreign key rather than by inference from timestamps. Results are immutable after insert, enforced by a trigger that rejects `UPDATE` on `results.text`; reprocessing inserts, never replaces. `recordings.display_run_id` is a user-movable pointer deciding what the list view shows.

## Persistence choice (D-005)

SQLite through GRDB with FTS5 over result text. History search is a stated requirement and FTS5 with bm25 ranking and snippets is why SQLite wins here; SwiftData and Core Data have no comparable text index and their migration behavior is harder to test. Schema versions are numbered migrations, each with a test that runs the migration against a fixture database captured at the prior version.

## Audio: journal, sealing, and artifacts (D-030)

Capture writes fixed-period chunks (default two seconds) of raw interleaved Int16 at the source's native rate into `journal/<stream>/`, each written to `<seq>.pcm.part`, fsynced, renamed to `<seq>.pcm`, with the directory fsynced. A chunk carries no header; its format lives in the fsynced manifest, so any complete chunk decodes on its own and a torn final chunk is discardable. A sealer running in the batch lane encodes completed chunks into Apple Lossless in CAF, appends `(chunk_seq, packet_count, byte_offset)` to `index.log` with an fsync, and deletes chunks whose packets are durably recorded, so transient journal storage stays near a 30-second window rather than the whole recording. At the end of capture the sealer writes the CAF packet table from `index.log`, fsyncs, records the artifact sha256, and the run commits.

The design does not assume a truncated container can be finalized. After a crash, recovery rebuilds the packet table from `index.log` up to the last durable entry, truncates the container to that extent, and appends any surviving chunks. The worst-case loss is the unsealed tail: at most one chunk period plus data the OS had not yet flushed within it. The exact bound is measured by the kill-at-offset experiment in verification, which has not been run; the chunk period is the tuning knob if it comes out worse than expected.

Canonical recognition format is 16 kHz mono Float32, produced by a converter stage from native frames rather than at the source port. Sealed dictation audio is 16 kHz mono ALAC at roughly 50 to 60 MB per hour by arithmetic from 16-bit PCM at 115 MB per hour; meeting streams are sealed at native rate, which is larger and reported in the library size view. Lossy encoding is rejected because re-recognition with a better model later is a requirement. Imported files are copied in their original encoding and decoded on demand.

## Settings snapshots and derived results

A mode is a named entity with an append-only chain of `mode_revisions`, each content-addressed over prompt, formatting rules, transformation contract, validator language list, and model selections. A run's manifest stores revision ids. Editing a mode creates a revision and leaves saved results pointing at the revision that produced them, which is what makes "later edits must not silently change the meaning of a saved result" structural. History shows the producing revision and diffs it against the current one.

## Context retention (D-016)

By default the store keeps a SHA-256 digest, byte length, and source kind per context sample in `context_digests`, not the text. That is enough to tell a user reprocessing an old recording that the original context is unavailable without retaining copies of unrelated documents and screens. Retaining the text is opt-in per mode, shown in History, and deleted with the recording.

## Interrupted operations (D-031)

Ordering rule: an externally visible irreversible effect is preceded by a durable record of intent (delivery), while a local idempotent effect is followed by its commit (sealing). Recovery at launch reconciles manifests, files, and rows by run state:

- `arming`: remove the session directory. No rows.
- `capturing`: seal the journal, commit the recording with `interrupted = true`, mark the run `cancelled(capturing, crash)`. Nothing is delivered; History offers recognition.
- `sealing`: a sealed artifact may exist without rows. Re-sealing is idempotent because it is derived from the journal and `index.log`, so recovery completes it and commits as above.
- `recognizing`: no partial transcript is saved; the run becomes `failed(recognizing, interrupted)`; audio is retained; History offers a new recognition run.
- `refining`: the recognition result is committed and immutable. Refining is a pure function of committed inputs pinned in the manifest, so recovery re-runs it, commits the normalized result, and stops. Recovery never resumes generation or delivery.
- `rewriting`: the run becomes `failed(rewriting, interrupted)`; the normalized result stands; History offers a rewrite run.
- `delivering`: any `delivery_attempts` row in `pending`, `posted`, or `posted_unconfirmed` becomes `needs_review`, the run becomes `delivery_unresolved`, and nothing is re-posted (D-010).
- Scratch directories, staged model directories, and model blobs with no referencing row and no live lease are removed. Leases with no live holder are reclaimed.

## Deletion during active processing (D-024, D-033)

Deletion sets `recordings.deleted_at`, increments `recordings.generation`, and signals cancellation to every lease holder. Each worker carries `(recording_id, generation)` from admission. A worker's commit is one transaction that re-reads the recording row and aborts if the row is missing, tombstoned, or at a different generation; on abort it removes its scratch directory and returns. The existence check and the insert cannot be separated, so a late response cannot recreate a deleted recording, and the generation counter covers delete-then-recreate at the same identifier.

Hard deletion of rows, artifacts, and FTS entries runs when the last lease on the recording is released, and again at launch. Until then the recording is hidden and reported as deleting rather than as reclaimed space.

## Retention (D-033)

Retention defaults to keeping everything. Optional age-based, size-based, and audio-discarding policies are ordinary deletion jobs: they acquire the same leases, observe the same generation checks, and skip any recording with a live lease held by a worker, a player, or an export, retrying on the next pass. Discarding audio moves `recordings.audio_state` to `audio_discarded`, which History displays; playback and re-recognition are then unavailable while text reprocessing remains available. The first run of any policy lists exactly what it would remove before removing it.

## Cancellation by run stage (D-007)

Cancellation has a defined effect at every stage and the panel names that effect when it happens. Cancelling one run never alters results committed by another run.

- `arming`: nothing captured; session directory removed; no rows.
- `capturing`: capture stops; the journal is discarded by default and no History row is created; a per-mode setting seals it as an interrupted recording instead.
- `recognizing`: the worker stops at its next checkpoint; audio is kept; the run is marked cancelled; no partial transcript is saved, because a truncated transcript that looks complete is worse than none.
- `refining`: the recognition result stands; the normalized result is dropped.
- `rewriting`: generation stops; the normalized result is kept and offered for delivery.
- `delivering`: cancellable until the first event is posted. After that the app reports that delivery was attempted and stops; it does not try to undo keystrokes in another application.

## Permissions as a capability matrix (D-032)

Revocation is handled per capability and per run state rather than by one global rule. Losing a capability terminates only the work that capability serves.

- Microphone denied at launch: recording controls disabled with a link to the settings pane; file import still works. Revoked during `capturing`: capture stops, the journal is sealed, the recording is marked interrupted, no delivery.
- Screen Recording denied: system audio and screen context unavailable; microphone recording, all modes, and rules that do not need screen context continue; meetings degrade to microphone only with a visible marker. Revoked during `capturing` of a meeting: the system stream ends and is marked truncated at a timestamp, the microphone stream continues, and the recording says which streams cover which interval.
- Accessibility denied or revoked: text insertion via selected text is unavailable and delivery falls back to the pasteboard path or to a held result; recognition and rewriting continue to completion. Revocation during `recognizing` does not stop recognition.
- Input Monitoring denied or revoked: the event tap cannot run, so push-to-talk is unavailable and toggle falls back to a Carbon hotkey; an in-flight run continues, and the panel gains a stop control.
- Automation for a browser denied: URL predicates do not match, evaluation continues, and the panel shows that the mode came from the fallback.
- Restoration: capabilities are re-probed on the relevant system notification and at each arming, and the panel reports the recovered capability once rather than on every session.

## Secure input

If `IsSecureEventInputEnabled()` is true at arming, the run records but is marked delivery-unavailable up front. If it becomes true by delivery time, the app posts no events, holds the result in History, offers copy, and says another application has secure input active. Password fields are the common case, and silently dropping text there would be the worst available failure.

## Delivery failures (D-008, D-009, D-010)

Insertion is defined in terms of caret and selection. The first rung sets `AXSelectedText` on the latched element, which inserts at the caret or replaces the user's selection; the app never sets `AXValue`, because that replaces a field's entire contents. Rungs are chosen from a capability probe taken at arming and re-checked at delivery.

- Selected-text insertion unsupported or the probe fails: fall to the pasteboard path.
- Pasteboard path with readable target state (value length or selected-text range): sample before and after Command-V and wait up to 500 ms for a change. Observed change means delivered. Observed absence of change means rejected, and only then is synthesized Unicode typing attempted, capped at 400 characters, above which the app holds and offers copy.
- Pasteboard path with unreadable target state: the outcome is unobservable. The attempt is recorded `posted_unconfirmed`, nothing is retried, and the panel offers Copy and Deliver again as user actions. Synthetic typing is never used after an unobservable outcome, because that is how a paragraph gets inserted twice.
- Pasteboard restore: attempted after the outcome is determined, never on a fixed timer relative to the paste, and only while `changeCount` still equals ours. For unobservable outcomes the restore is deferred by a per-application profile delay, default 750 ms, and the panel offers Restore now. Applications measured to read the pasteboard late have restore disabled in their profile, with the panel stating that the dictated text is still on the pasteboard.
- Pasteboard cannot be snapshotted (over 10 MB, promised files, unsupported types): the user is told before anything is written and chooses between proceeding without restore and copy-only.
- Focus moved to another application by delivery time: hold, and show a card with the text, Deliver, and Copy. Re-activating the latched application first is opt-in because it steals focus.
- Focus moved within the same application: deliver into the current element by default (per-mode toggle), matching the common case of clicking into the field while speaking.
- Latched application quit: hold and offer copy.
- Submit modifier: the Return is posted only when the modifier was held at stop, delivery went to the latched element, and the path posted events. A held or unconfirmed delivery never auto-submits.

## Model and runtime failures (D-022)

- Download interrupted or hash mismatch: the staging directory is removed, no blob is created, the active installation is untouched, and the error names expected and computed digests.
- User-supplied model failing the load smoke test: it stays in staging with the error attached; nothing is activated.
- Helper crash during generation: the client observes the socket close, marks the run failed with the exit status, keeps the recognition and normalized results, and offers retry. Three crashes on one installation mark it suspect in the model list.
- Model blob missing for a pinned run: the run fails at the stage that needed it and points at the model manager. Loading never falls back to downloading.
- Pairing exceeding the residency budget: refused at activation with the arithmetic shown, and the refusal states whether the numbers are measured or declared. The user can override, because it is their machine.

## Resource and storage failures

- Disk full during capture: capture stops, the journal is sealed to the last complete chunk, the recording is marked interrupted, and the panel reports the reason.
- Journal fsync failing repeatedly: capture stops rather than continuing with an unrecoverable tail.
- Unsupported import format: the source is untouched, the session directory is removed, and the error names the format and the optional external decoder path (D-018, D-028).
- Audio device removed mid-run: capture stops and the recording is sealed as interrupted; the app does not silently switch devices under an active recording.

## Desktop restore failures (D-025)

The app can observe that some audio client is running on the default output device and can post a play-pause key; neither identifies the application that reacted. Automatic resume is therefore off by default: after recording, the menu and panel offer Resume playback as a user action for ten minutes. When the user enables automatic resume, it fires only if the app posted the pause, the same output device is still default, the device is still idle, and under ten minutes have elapsed, and the menu records that the app cannot confirm which application it addressed. Input device volume is restored only if the current value still equals the value the app set; any mismatch means no restore and a note that the setting was left as found.

## Gate-based plan

Every phase lists entry gates, persisted-schema work, the failure cases it must handle, the evidence that closes it, the reviewer who approves that evidence (D-035), and what a rollback costs. Feasibility work that can invalidate a boundary runs before that boundary is frozen (D-034).

**Phase F, feasibility, before ports and schema are frozen.** Entry: none. Work: four spikes with thin adapters. F1 speech runtime harness (both candidates where licensing permits): word error rate on a fixed corpus, time to final transcript, helper peak RSS at 10 minutes, 1 hour, and 3 hours, cancellation latency, and whether resuming from a window checkpoint reproduces the unpreempted transcript. F2 helper isolation: launch a helper under the strictest available process restriction, assert an outbound connect fails, and assert the linked binary and its dependency closure reference no networking symbols. F3 crash-safe capture: kill the writer at randomized offsets, recover, and record the maximum lost interval and any index corruption. F4 insertion prototype: selected-text insertion and paste with readback in TextEdit, Mail, Safari plain and contenteditable, Chrome, Terminal, Xcode, VS Code, Slack, and Figma, recording which paths preserve existing content and which give an observable signal. Schema: none. Evidence: capability descriptors, a loss bound, an insertion matrix, and decision records updating D-020, D-028, D-030, D-009, D-004, D-027. Rollback: each spike has a named fallback (whisper.cpp as the reference runtime, the narrowed egress claim, a shorter chunk period, hold-and-copy delivery), so a negative result changes parameters rather than the architecture.

**Phase 0, skeleton.** Entry: F1 descriptors, F3 loss bound, F4 matrix. Work: package layout, ports including timestamped frames and flow control, the full run state machine, schema v1 with runs, results, leases, tombstones, generations, the recovery table, the recording panel shell, fake audio source, fake recognizer, fake inserter. Schema: v1. Failures: cancel at every stage, kill at every stage boundary, delete during processing, retention racing a lease. Evidence: the lifetime running end to end on fakes with the recovery outcomes asserted per state, plus approved behavior tables for the run machine. Rollback: none downstream, which is why it is first.

**Phase 1, capture and delivery.** Entry: phase 0 exit, F4 matrix. Work: microphone source, chunk journal and sealer, software input gain with metering and clipping indication, shortcut registrar with separate toggle and push-to-talk bindings, insertion ladder, pasteboard policy, focus policy, permission matrix, menu bar item. Schema: v2 adds `delivery_attempts` profile fields and per-application delivery profiles. Failures: permission revocation per capability, secure input, unobservable paste, unsnapshotable pasteboard, lost key-up. Evidence: the delivery matrix run by hand and dated, plus automated permission-matrix tests. Rollback: removing a rung is a profile change.

**Phase 2, speech runtime.** Entry: F1 selection and licensing review. Work: the chosen adapter behind `SpeechRecognizer`, recognition results persisted, History list with playback. Schema: v3 adds `segments` and recognition parameters. Failures: model missing, helper crash, cancellation mid-window. Evidence: word error rate rows attached to machine, model revision, and quantization; the memory slope test at three durations. Rollback: the second adapter, if F1 kept one.

**Phase 3, vocabulary and the Standard mode.** Entry: phase 2. Work: the four-stage vocabulary pipeline, the Standard built-in mode, `TextValidation` with the English pack. Schema: v4 adds `vocabulary_revisions` and normalized results. Failures: fail-closed on a language with no pack. Evidence: table-driven determinism tests and approved behavior tables for each stage.

**Phase 4, generation and modes.** Entry: phase 3, F2 outcome. Work: the generation helper, Email and Note modes, prompt assembly, transformation contracts, the custom mode editor with revisions. Schema: v5 adds `mode_revisions` contract fields and rewritten results. Failures: validator fallback, helper crash, injection corpus. Evidence: human rubric scores on the fidelity corpus including adversarial cases, and per-mode fallback rates.

**Phase 5, model library.** Entry: phase 4. Work: content-addressed blobs, staged verification, smoke tests, transactional activation, leases, garbage collection, user-supplied imports, offline enforcement checks. Schema: v6 adds `model_installations` and `active_models`. Failures: crash between rename and commit, activation while a run is pinned, failed import. Evidence: crash-injection around activation and a network-denied full session.

**Phase 6, automatic mode selection and context.** Entry: phase 4. Work: the rule engine, the three context sources, degraded states. Schema: v7 adds `context_digests` and rules. Evidence: a dated browser URL matrix and rule-shadowing tests.

**Phase 7, input sources.** Entry: phase 2 memory slope result. Work: system audio, audio and video import, seekable decoding with credit-based flow control, the format matrix, the optional external decoder with its trust statement. Schema: v8 adds `audio_artifacts.role` values and import provenance. Failures: unsupported format, failed import leaving the source untouched, backpressure on a slow recognizer. Evidence: helper and app RSS at 10 minutes, 1 hour, and 3 hours with the slope reported.

**Phase 8, meetings.** Entry: phase 7, plus the diarizer decision for the diarization half. Work: dual-stream capture with host-time alignment, channel-labeled transcripts, timestamped notes with citations. Diarization, cluster identities, and speaker naming ship only after the diarizer is selected, licensed, and evaluated; until then meetings ship with channel labels. Schema: v9 adds clusters, identities, assignments. Evidence: alignment drift measurements and, for diarization, diarization error rate plus the below-threshold rate.

**Phase 9, languages and retention.** Entry: phase 4, phase 5. Work: language selection and detection, translation as a derived result, additional validator packs, retention policies over the lease protocol, the evaluation harness. Schema: v10 adds translation results and retention settings. Evidence: per-language word error rate rows and a retention-versus-lease race test.

**Phase 10, desktop integration completion.** Entry: phase 1. Work: media pause with manual resume, optional automatic resume behind its ownership conditions, hardware input volume as an opt-in, per-application delivery profiles surfaced in settings. Schema: v11 adds desktop preferences. Evidence: a manual matrix over Music, Spotify, a browser tab, and a video conferencing application, recording what paused and what resumed.

## Adding a new input source

A new source implements `AudioSource`, emitting timestamped native frames plus a `SourceDescriptor` (live or seekable, clock domain, known duration, native rate and channel layout, whether it honors credit). Only arming branches on live versus seekable, because a live source latches a delivery target and a file source does not. The alternative considered was a pipeline per source, with each owning its chunking, conversion, and cancellation. That is shorter today and duplicates the parts most likely to be wrong: a memory bug on long input would exist only in the import path, and cancellation semantics would drift between paths. The cost of one port is that every source must carry timing metadata even when it has one stream and no drift.

## Replacing a model runtime

Runtimes are separate adapter targets and helper binaries, each publishing a capability descriptor with measured fields and a parameter schema. `results.params_json` stores parameters under a stable application-level schema with a runtime-specific extension blob, so History rows from an old runtime remain readable after a swap. The settings interface renders common parameters (context length, temperature, beam size, thread count, quantization) generically from that schema, and runtimes may supply presentation hooks for parameters with conditional validity, model-specific ranges, or memory effects. Replacing a runtime therefore adds a small amount of interface work rather than none (D-202); the earlier claim that it adds no bespoke UI was too strong.

Calling the runtime API directly from feature code removes a layer. Under it, swapping runtimes touches every call site, the settings interface, and the persisted parameters, and old History rows referencing removed parameter names become uninterpretable. Since RESEARCH flags the speech runtime choice as unresolved on licensing, long-recording behavior, and integration cost, designing as though the first choice is permanent would be the wrong bet.

Storage effect of a swap is bounded by the content-addressed blob store: each installation is referenced by rows that name a runtime kind, so the model manager shows per-runtime totals and can release a runtime's blobs once nothing references them.

## Maintenance costs accepted

- GRDB: a dependency with its own cadence plus migration discipline, paid for by FTS5 and tested migrations.
- Vendored C or C++ runtimes: long builds, periodic vendoring, and upstream API drift. Pinned to tagged revisions with an update checklist that reruns the evaluation harness and refreshes capability descriptors.
- `CGEventTap` and accessibility insertion: per-application behavior is undocumented and changes. The delivery matrix is re-run per macOS minor release and per major update of the applications in it, and the result is a dated table in the repository.
- Validator language packs: each new language needs segmentation, interrogative detection, and a content-word list, plus rubric review in that language. Languages without a pack are handled by the fail-closed path rather than by an untested check.
- Chunk journal: extra file management and an fsync every chunk period, plus a sealer to maintain. It is the price of a recovery story that does not depend on a container surviving a kill.
- Media key posting: it can break silently. Manual resume as the default means a break degrades to nothing happening.

## What supporting other Macs would require

Intel support means a CPU-capable speech adapter, a smaller generation model, its own memory budget, and its own evaluation run; RESEARCH notes that documented platform support does not establish comparable performance. Machines with 8 GB need a smaller pairing and a residency policy that unloads the speech model before loading the generation model, at the cost of latency between stages. Both are adapter and policy changes.

## Who decides what correct means (D-035)

A passing test shows the implementation met its assertions under the tested conditions; the assertions can encode a wrong expectation. Expected behavior is therefore written and approved before tests are written. `docs/behavior/` holds a table per subsystem giving, for each (state, event) pair, the expected next state, the persisted effect, and the user-visible effect. Cancellation, permission loss per capability, focus change, crash at each boundary, lease conflict, and validator fallback are events in those tables. Every row cites a SPEC.md clause; rows with no clause are marked derived and need explicit approval. The normative approver is the user as product owner, or a delegate named in `docs/behavior/OWNERS`; independent authorship is a hygiene rule and not the authority. Tests reference row identifiers, and changing an approved row requires re-approval recorded in git history.

## Automated checks

- Run state machine property tests over every (state, event) pair including generated random sequences, asserting invariants: no delivery without a previously committed `delivery_attempts` row; no results row for a run cancelled before `sealing`; an artifact exists on disk exactly when its row says so; `results.text` is never updated; every non-recognition result has a `derived_from_result_id` belonging to the same recording.
- Provenance tests: re-recognize a recording under a second speech model, then rewrite and translate from each recognition result, and assert that every artifact resolves to exactly one recognition result and one model installation.
- Crash injection: SIGKILL at each stage boundary, relaunch, and assert the recovery outcome named in the approved table for that state, including no automatic re-delivery after a kill during `delivering` and idempotent re-sealing after a kill during `sealing`.
- Kill-at-offset capture experiment: randomized kills during capture across chunk boundaries and mid-fsync, measuring the maximum lost interval and asserting the container plus index always yields a decodable artifact. This is the measurement that replaces the earlier assumption that a truncated container can be finalized; it has not been run.
- Deletion and retention races: a deterministic scheduler test that deletes a recording, and separately runs an age policy and an audio-discard policy, while a worker and a player hold leases; asserts commits abort, no rows appear, scratch is removed, retention defers, and playback is not interrupted.
- Long-input memory: import at 10 minutes, 1 hour, and 3 hours, sampling resident size of the app and of the recognition helper across each run, asserting a per-duration ceiling and that the fitted slope of peak RSS against duration is within measurement noise. Measuring one duration in one process cannot establish that memory is independent of duration.
- Offline enforcement: a complete session including model load under a network-denied profile, plus a build check that helper targets and their dependency closure import no networking modules, a symbol scan of the linked binaries, and a static check failing the build if a runtime is constructed through an initializer that can download.
- Prompt-injection corpus: clipboard and screen context containing instruction-shaped text, asserting the contract validator holds, the transcript survives, and no span of eight or more tokens present in context and absent from the transcript appears in the output.
- Validator language behavior: for each mode and language pair without a pack, assert the run falls back to the normalized transcript, records the reason, and delivers nothing unvalidated unless the per-mode override is set.
- Vocabulary determinism: ordering, ICU word boundaries, case handling, scripts without spaces, and post-generation reapplication, table-driven.
- Model activation: crash injection between blob rename and the activation transaction, activation while a run holds a lease on the previous installation, and garbage collection with and without live leases.
- Schema migration from fixture databases at each prior version.
- Panel placement restore across display reconfiguration, including a removed display and an off-screen frame.

## Human review where assertions are weak

Transformation fidelity is reviewed, not only asserted. A fixed corpus of recordings has expected outputs per mode, scored against a rubric: meaning preserved, no invented facts, questions still questions, vocabulary terms intact, formatting within the declared contract. The corpus includes adversarial cases built to pass lexical checks while changing meaning: removed or inserted negation, swapped quantities, modality changes such as must to may, swapped attribution between two named people, an answer appended after a retained question, and a sentence copied from the context block. Cross-language cases cover each shipped validator pack. The reviewer is not the author of the mode under review, and the approver of the expected outputs is the product owner.

Practical behavior in other applications is verified by running the delivery matrix by hand across TextEdit, Mail, Notes, Safari plain input and contenteditable, Chrome, Xcode, Terminal, VS Code, Slack, Messages, and Figma. Each cell records: whether selected-text insertion is supported and whether it preserved existing field content; insertion at a caret in the middle of existing text; replacement of an active selection; paste with a delayed consumer; pasteboard restore outcome, including targets that read late and unsnapshotable content; non-Latin text covering Japanese, Arabic in a right-to-left field, combining marks, and emoji; behavior with an input method active; secure fields; and focus changing while events are being posted. The table is dated and re-run on macOS updates.

## Measurement protocols that have not been run

No benchmark here has been executed. Each protocol is defined so results, when they exist, are attributable.

- Recognition: word error rate by language on a public set and an internal set, recording machine model, memory, macOS version, runtime revision, model revision and quantization, and audio characteristics. Recognition is scored separately from rewriting, because a rewrite rubric cannot distinguish a mis-recognized word from a badly reworded sentence.
- Latency: stop to delivered text, split into recognition and generation, at three durations, reported as a distribution over repeated runs.
- Runtime capability descriptors: cancellation latency at p50 and p95, transcript equivalence after preemption and resume, peak process RSS and Metal heap peak per model installation.
- Diarization: diarization error rate on a labeled internal meeting set, the proportion of segments below the attribution threshold, and performance under speaker echo when headphones are not used.
- Meeting notes: rubric scoring against the audio, with citation validity checked automatically and the uncited-bullet drop rate tracked.

Until a measurement exists, the interface reports language support as declared by the model publisher and marked unmeasured, and no latency claim appears in the product.
assumptions: Deployment baseline is provisionally macOS 14.0. Basis: RESEARCH records macOS 14 and Xcode 16 among the Argmax Swift package prerequisites, and ScreenCaptureKit system-audio capture predates 14. The floor derives from a runtime that has not been selected, so it is a planning value. Reconsider at gate F1, which reports the minimum API set actually used; if the shipping runtime does not need 14, the floor drops, and if combined microphone plus system capture through one ScreenCaptureKit stream becomes necessary for meeting alignment, it rises.

Apple Silicon with 16 GB is the evaluation target and Intel is unsupported in the first release. Basis: stated in the specification. RESEARCH notes whisper.cpp supports Intel, so a CPU-capable adapter keeps the option open without a structural change. Reconsider when an Intel requirement is confirmed; the work is a memory budget, a model pairing, and a separate evaluation run.

Model residency fits an 8 GB application budget on the 16 GB target: a turbo-class speech model at roughly 0.8 to 1.6 GB of weights, an 8B-class generation model at 4-bit quantization at roughly 4.5 to 5 GB, plus a few hundred MB of KV cache at 8k context. Basis: published quantized file sizes and standard KV arithmetic, with no measured resident size and no accounting for runtime workspaces or Metal heaps. Reconsider at the first F1 descriptor, which reports process RSS and Metal peak; refusals state whether their numbers are measured or declared.

The application ships unsandboxed with hardened runtime and Developer ID notarization. Basis: setting selected text on other applications' accessibility elements and running a session-level event tap are not available to a sandboxed application without exceptions granted outside the Mac App Store. Reconsider if App Store distribution becomes a goal, which removes push-to-talk and the accessibility insertion path rather than merely changing them.

Build checks plus a network-denied session test are the enforceable form of the offline guarantee until gate F2 reports otherwise. Basis: a symbol scan and a dependency-closure check cannot prove that a system framework or dynamically loaded code performs no request, and the specification's own open question records that per-process restriction mechanisms may be unavailable. Reconsider when F2 demonstrates an enforceable process restriction, at which point the product claim strengthens from tested absence to system-enforced denial.

The maximum audio loss after an abrupt termination is one chunk period plus unflushed data within it. Basis: chunks are written, fsynced, and renamed individually, and the packet index is appended and fsynced, so recovery depends on the app's own durable records rather than on a container surviving truncation. The exact bound has not been measured. Reconsider after the kill-at-offset experiment in phase F; a worse bound is answered by shortening the chunk period, which costs more fsyncs.

Prompt-based vocabulary biasing in the whisper family raises the chance a term is recognized and guarantees nothing. Basis: the mechanism is a decoder prompt rather than a decoding constraint, and the prompt slot is bounded at roughly 224 tokens. The product text says exactly this. Reconsider if a runtime exposes real biasing or constrained decoding, which moves exact-name handling into recognition.

Lexical and structural validator checks are necessary conditions on transformation fidelity, not a proof that a mode obeyed its contract. Basis: content-word recall, interrogative survival, expansion ratio, and context n-gram overlap can all pass on text whose meaning changed. Reconsider if the adversarial fidelity corpus finds a class of violations that survives every check, which would argue for a sampled semantic check by a second model despite its cost and its shared failure mode.

Basis: it is a public property needing no private framework, and it identifies neither the playing application nor the effect of a posted media key. This is why automatic resume is off by default. AVFoundation covers the initial import format matrix: wav, aiff, caf, mp3, m4a in AAC and ALAC, mp4, m4v, and mov. Basis: system decoder coverage. Reconsider at the first refusal, with opus in webm and matroska the likely ones, at which point the user-selected external decoder is the documented path and its trust transfer is stated plainly.

decisions.title: macOS baseline and hardware target, held provisional until the runtime is selected
decisions.choice: Plan against deployment target macOS 14.0 and Apple Silicon for the first release, with later-OS APIs gated at runtime and never required. Treat the floor as provisional and set it from the minimum API set that gate F1 reports the shipping runtime actually needs.
decisions.rationale: RESEARCH records macOS 14 and Xcode 16 as prerequisites of one candidate speech runtime, and that runtime is not selected. Deriving a permanent floor from an unselected dependency would fix a constraint for a reason that may disappear. ScreenCaptureKit system-audio capture is available at 14, the WWDC24 microphone stream output arrived later, and microphone capture uses AVAudioEngine on every supported version so the newer output is off the critical path. The specification names Apple Silicon with 16 GB as the evaluation target.

alternatives.option: Baseline macOS 15 for the unified ScreenCaptureKit microphone plus system-audio stream
alternatives.tradeoff: One capture path and a shared clock for meetings, at the cost of excluding Sonoma users for a convenience the two-stream design handles with host-time alignment.

alternatives.option: Baseline macOS 13
alternatives.tradeoff: Wider reach; falls below one candidate runtime's stated prerequisite and adds an OS to the support matrix that nothing is evaluated on.

alternatives.option: Ship Intel and Apple Silicon together
alternatives.tradeoff: Broader hardware coverage; doubles the evaluation burden that RESEARCH warns documentation cannot substitute for, and forces a second model tier before the primary target is measured.

decisions.consequences: Meetings align two streams by host time rather than receiving them from one. Intel users wait for a CPU-capable adapter and its own evaluation. Any API newer than the final floor sits behind an availability check with a defined fallback, and the floor is recorded as a decision output of phase F rather than an input.
decisions.reconsider_when: F1 reports the shipping runtime's real minimum, an Intel requirement is confirmed, or measured two-stream drift makes a single-stream capture path necessary.

decisions.title: Package layout and dependency direction
decisions.choice: One SPM package with a pure core, a ports target of protocols and value types, a validation target holding transformation contracts and language packs, adapter targets per external concern, and a thin Xcode app shell as the composition root. Core depends only on ports; nothing depends on an adapter except the shell.
decisions.rationale: The scope includes a speech runtime that is not yet chosen, four input sources, and an insertion mechanism whose behavior varies per target application. Each is an adapter. Keeping the run state machine, mode resolution, vocabulary pipeline, and contract validation free of system frameworks is what allows phase 0 to exercise cancel, crash, delete-during-processing, and retention races before any runtime exists.

alternatives.option: Single application target with feature folders
alternatives.tradeoff: Faster early progress; every behavioral test then needs permissions and real models, and swapping a runtime touches feature code throughout.

alternatives.option: Separate SPM packages per subsystem in a workspace
alternatives.tradeoff: Stronger boundaries and independent versioning, at the cost of cross-package version churn for a single application with one consumer.

decisions.consequences: Adapters need explicit wiring in the shell and value types at the boundary rather than framework types passed around. The `.app` cannot come from `swift build` alone, so there are two entry points: `swift test` for logic and the Xcode scheme for the shipping application.
decisions.reconsider_when: The port boundary starts needing per-adapter escape hatches that leak framework types into core, which would mean the abstraction is fighting the domain.

decisions.title: Inference runs in child helper processes, not in-process and not behind a local HTTP server
decisions.choice: Generation runs in `dictation-llm-helper`, launched by the app and reached over an inherited socket pair with a length-prefixed protocol. Speech recognition uses the same pattern when the runtime is a C or C++ library. Nothing listens on a TCP port.
decisions.rationale: RESEARCH notes llama.cpp ships server tooling beside library integration material and asks that process ownership and network reachability be treated as a design concern. A local HTTP endpoint binds a port every process on the machine can reach, needs its own authentication, and is the component most likely to acquire forwarding behavior through configuration the app does not own. Crash isolation is the second reason: a quantization that faults the runtime should not take the user's in-flight transcript with it. Residency accounting is the third: model memory lives in a process the parent can measure and terminate.

alternatives.option: Link the runtime into the application process
alternatives.tradeoff: Lowest latency and no IPC; a native crash kills the app mid-run, and address-space growth from model loading persists for the process lifetime.

alternatives.option: Run the upstream HTTP server on localhost
alternatives.tradeoff: Reuses upstream tooling and its API; opens a port to all local processes and turns the offline property into an operational claim about configuration.

alternatives.option: XPC service in the app bundle
alternatives.tradeoff: System-managed lifecycle and a typed interface; launchd-managed restarts complicate residency accounting, and streaming large audio windows and token output over a socket the app owns is more direct.

decisions.consequences: A serialization boundary and a lifecycle to manage. Streaming tokens for live rewrite feedback needs a chunked message type. Audio windows cross a process boundary, so the memory ceiling must be measured in the helper as well as the app.
decisions.reconsider_when: IPC overhead measurably dominates generation latency for short dictations, or a runtime gains a supported in-process Swift API with equivalent crash isolation.

decisions.title: Concurrency model and resource scheduling from measured runtime capabilities
decisions.choice: One actor per processing run owning its state and rows; a real-time audio callback writing into lock-free rings; a single `ResourceScheduler` actor with capture, interactive, and batch lanes admitting at most one speech job and one generation job. Preemption policy is read from each runtime's measured capability descriptor: yield at a safe checkpoint where the runtime supports it, otherwise cancel and restart from the last committed checkpoint or let the batch job finish behind a displayed bound. Until descriptors exist, use cancel-and-restart.
decisions.rationale: The scope puts a latency-sensitive dictation path beside long batch work on a machine that cannot hold several models resident, so an admission policy is needed and is better in one testable place than invented by the first task that hits contention. The earlier version assumed both runtimes could checkpoint and resume without changing output; nothing in RESEARCH establishes that. Making resumability a measured descriptor field means the scheduler is implementable for whichever runtime ships, and the conservative default is correct for both.

alternatives.option: Unstructured concurrency with a global lock around model access
alternatives.tradeoff: Less code; priority inversion when a three-hour import holds the lock while the user dictates, with no clean preemption point.

alternatives.option: Serial queue, first come first served
alternatives.tradeoff: Predictable; the user waits behind a batch job, which is the failure the requirements care about most.

alternatives.option: Concurrent speech and generation residency with no admission control
alternatives.tradeoff: Better pipelining on a large machine; on the 16 GB target it invites swap, turning a latency problem into a system-wide stall.

decisions.consequences: Batch workers need resumable checkpoints regardless of policy, since cancel-and-restart still needs a restart point. The provisional pass is an admitted job that can be denied, so the panel has a preview-paused state. The audio callback thread has hard constraints that need review discipline. Descriptor values become part of shipped data and are refreshed when a runtime is updated.
decisions.reconsider_when: Descriptors show a runtime whose resume reproduces the unpreempted transcript, allowing true preemption, or measurements show a machine class where concurrent residency fits and the single-job rule costs latency for nothing.

decisions.title: Persistence: SQLite with FTS5 for metadata and text, files for audio
decisions.choice: SQLite through GRDB in WAL mode for metadata, runs, results, leases, and result text, with FTS5 over result text; audio in per-recording directories. Numbered migrations with fixture-based migration tests.
decisions.rationale: History requires search across transcripts and results, and FTS5 with bm25 ranking and snippets is the reason to prefer SQLite. Deletion during active work, lease acquisition, and model activation all need a transaction that combines a check with a write. Keeping audio out of the database keeps its backup, integrity check, and migration times short.

alternatives.option: SwiftData
alternatives.tradeoff: Least code for models and views with native observation; no full-text index, and migration behavior is harder to test against fixtures for a schema that must survive eleven phases.

alternatives.option: Core Data with an external search index
alternatives.tradeoff: Mature and Apple-supported; adds a second index to keep consistent with deletions, which is the consistency problem the tombstone and lease rules exist to contain.

alternatives.option: Raw libsqlite3 with a hand-written wrapper
alternatives.tradeoff: No third-party dependency; reimplements migrations, statement caching, and observation, which is where maintenance accumulates.

alternatives.option: JSON files per recording with an in-memory index
alternatives.tradeoff: Inspectable and easy to back up; search, leases, and transactional deletion become bespoke, and the index is rebuilt every launch.

decisions.consequences: A dependency with its own release cadence and migration discipline. FTS triggers must stay in sync with result inserts and deletes, covered by tests. Database and files can disagree after a crash, which the recovery contract resolves.
decisions.reconsider_when: The system SQLite lacks FTS5 on the baseline, in which case GRDB is built against a bundled SQLite, or library sizes make a per-recording file layout with an external index preferable.

decisions.title: Processing runs as explicit state machines with a per-run settings snapshot
decisions.choice: A state machine per processing run (idle, arming, capturing, sealing, recognizing, refining, rewriting, delivering, terminal) in the pure core, with a `RunManifest` written and fsynced at run start pinning mode revision, model installation ids, vocabulary revision, language setting, translation flag, validator pack, and, for reprocessing, the parent result id. Capture stages belong only to runs that capture.
decisions.rationale: Component boundaries follow this sequence. The manifest is what makes settings snapshots real: a run reads its manifest and never live settings, so editing a mode or switching models mid-run cannot change what a result means. The same manifest is what a reprocess copies and mutates and what recovery reads after a crash. Attaching the machine to a run rather than to a recording is what lets one recording carry several recognitions without ambiguity.

alternatives.option: Read live settings at each stage
alternatives.tradeoff: No snapshot machinery; a mode edit during a long recognition silently changes the result's meaning, which the requirements forbid.

alternatives.option: Implicit state through nullable columns
alternatives.tradeoff: Fewer types; illegal states become representable and per-stage cancellation loses its single definition point.

alternatives.option: One state machine per recording
alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler list view; a second recognition has nowhere to live and reprocessing has to mutate the recording's state.

decisions.consequences: Every new capability declares where it sits in the sequence and what cancellation there means. Settings changes take effect on the next run, which the interface must show so it does not read as a bug. History shows runs, which is more structure in the detail view than a flat result list.
decisions.reconsider_when: A requirement needs mid-run settings changes, such as switching language during a long meeting, which would need a segmented manifest rather than one per run.

decisions.title: Cancellation contract defined per run stage
decisions.choice: A stage-indexed table of cancellation effects enforced in core and shown in the panel: arming discards everything; capturing discards the journal by default with an opt-in to seal it as interrupted; recognizing keeps audio and saves no partial transcript; refining drops the normalized result; rewriting keeps the normalized result and offers it; delivering is cancellable only before the first event is posted. Cancelling a reprocess run leaves every earlier run's results intact.
decisions.rationale: The specification requires defined effects at every processing stage. Two judgment calls: recognizing saves no partial transcript because a truncated transcript that looks complete is more damaging than an absent one, and rewriting keeps the normalized result because the expensive work is done and the user usually still wants their words.

alternatives.option: Cancel always discards everything
alternatives.tradeoff: One rule; throws away a completed recognition because the user did not want the rewrite, which is the most common late cancel.

alternatives.option: Cancel always keeps everything
alternatives.tradeoff: Nothing is lost; a sentence spoken into the wrong window persists to History, which is a privacy surprise.

alternatives.option: Prompt at cancel time
alternatives.tradeoff: No wrong default; a modal on the escape path is when a user least wants a dialog.

decisions.consequences: Workers need checkpoints so cancel is prompt without being abrupt. The panel needs a per-stage message so the effect is visible when it happens rather than discovered later in History.
decisions.reconsider_when: Usage shows repeated re-recording after cancels during recognition, which would argue for keeping partial transcripts clearly marked as partial.

decisions.title: Delivery target latched at arming with an explicit focus-change policy
decisions.choice: At arming, latch the frontmost PID, bundle identifier, window number, focused accessibility element, and that element's insertion capability. At delivery: same element delivers; same application with a different element delivers by default under a per-mode toggle; a different application holds and shows a card with Deliver and Copy; a departed application holds. Re-focusing the latched target is opt-in. Only capture-initiated dictation runs deliver; reprocessing runs never auto-deliver.
decisions.rationale: The intended target is the one the user was looking at when they started speaking, and the panel is non-activating (D-011) so showing it does not disturb the latch. Holding rather than inserting into an unexpected application is conservative for a good reason: text placed in the wrong window can be unrecoverable and can be sensitive, while a hold costs one click.

alternatives.option: Always deliver into whatever is frontmost at delivery time
alternatives.tradeoff: No held results; text lands in the wrong application whenever focus changes during processing, which is common on longer recognitions.

alternatives.option: Always re-activate the latched application
alternatives.tradeoff: Matches intent most of the time; pulls focus away from whatever the user chose to do next, sometimes seconds later.

alternatives.option: Always hold and require confirmation
alternatives.tradeoff: Never wrong; adds a click to every dictation, which defeats the tool.

decisions.consequences: The panel needs a held state with actions and History must show undelivered results. The same-application default will occasionally insert into a different field in the same window, which is accepted because it matches clicking into the target field while speaking.
decisions.reconsider_when: Holds fire often enough to annoy, which would argue for making opt-in re-focus the default for users who enable it, or for shortening processing so focus changes are rarer.

decisions.title: Insertion ladder defined by caret and selection, with named observable signals
decisions.choice: Rung 1 sets `AXSelectedText` on the latched element, inserting at the caret or replacing the current selection, confirmed by reading back the selected-text range or value length. `AXValue` is never set, because that replaces a field's entire contents. Rung 2 writes the pasteboard and posts Command-V; where the target exposes readable value or range state, sample before and after and wait up to 500 ms for a change, treating an observed change as delivered and an observed absence as rejected. Rung 3, synthesized Unicode typing capped at 400 characters, runs only after an observed rejection. When the target exposes no readable state, the paste outcome is recorded `posted_unconfirmed`, nothing further is attempted, and the panel offers Copy and Deliver again. Pasteboard restore happens after the outcome is determined, only while the change count is ours, deferred by a per-application profile delay (default 750 ms) for unconfirmed outcomes, and disabled entirely for targets measured to read the pasteboard late.
decisions.rationale: The earlier ladder had two defects. Setting a value is destructive for any element holding existing text, and falling through to typing on a rejected paste requires a rejection signal the design had not named while also stating that paste success cannot be confirmed. Splitting targets into readable and unreadable resolves both: readable targets give a real signal that makes both the fallthrough and the restore safe, and unreadable targets get a single attempt with no retry, which is the only behavior that cannot duplicate text.

alternatives.option: Pasteboard and Command-V only
alternatives.tradeoff: One path to maintain; always disturbs the pasteboard, including where selected-text insertion would be clean and confirmable.

alternatives.option: Synthetic typing only
alternatives.tradeoff: Never touches the pasteboard; slow for long text, drops characters under load in some targets, and interleaves badly with user typing.

alternatives.option: A dedicated input method
alternatives.tradeoff: The system-supported route for inserting text, avoiding both the pasteboard and event synthesis; requires the user to install and select an input method, changing their typing setup for a dictation feature.

alternatives.option: Keep a fixed short restore delay
alternatives.tradeoff: Simple and usually invisible; races targets that read the pasteboard after the delay, pasting whatever the app restored.

decisions.consequences: Per-application profiles become shipped data with a maintenance obligation and a dated matrix. Some targets will never confirm delivery, so `posted_unconfirmed` is a normal outcome the interface must explain rather than an error. Restore is best-effort and says when it was skipped.
decisions.reconsider_when: The insertion prototype in phase F finds a readable signal for targets currently classed unreadable, or a supported API for inserting text into another application appears.

decisions.title: Delivery idempotency and no automatic retry
decisions.choice: Commit a `delivery_attempts` row (recording, result, run, target, state) before posting any event. States are pending, posted, posted_unconfirmed, held, failed. On launch, pending, posted, and posted_unconfirmed become needs_review. The app never re-posts automatically; re-delivery is a user action.
decisions.rationale: Paste into an unreadable target gives no confirmation, so after a crash the app cannot distinguish delivered from about to deliver. Any automatic retry risks inserting the same paragraph twice into someone's document. Committing the attempt before posting means recovery always sees that an attempt was in flight, and needs_review surfaces it without acting.

alternatives.option: Retry pending deliveries on launch
alternatives.tradeoff: Recovers a crash before posting; duplicates text after posting, with no way to tell the cases apart.

alternatives.option: No attempt record, recover from run state
alternatives.tradeoff: One fewer table; the window between deciding to deliver and posting is exactly where a crash is unrecoverable without a durable record.

alternatives.option: Confirm by reading the target back for every path
alternatives.tradeoff: Would allow safe retry; unavailable in the targets that need the paste path most, so it cannot be the general rule.

decisions.consequences: After a crash mid-delivery the user gets a needs_review item and decides. Re-delivery is always explicit, one extra interaction in a rare case.
decisions.reconsider_when: The readable-target class covers the common applications well enough that a bounded automatic retry is safe for those targets specifically.

decisions.title: Recording display as a non-activating panel with provisional and final states distinguished
decisions.choice: An NSPanel with nonactivating and borderless style, status-bar level, joining all spaces, movable by background, ordered front without becoming key. Provisional text renders in a secondary style with a live label; the final transcript replaces it in the primary style with a brief change highlight. The waveform is drawn from a 10 ms RMS and peak envelope computed allocation-free on the capture thread. Failures appear as a row with a short reason and one action. Placement is stored as a fraction of the display's visible frame plus the display identifier, clamped to the primary display when either is gone.
decisions.rationale: The panel must never become key, since activating it would break the delivery latch that D-008 depends on. Provisional and final text are different artifacts, so they are shown differently rather than silently swapped, and the provisional stream is never persisted as a result. Fractional placement survives resolution and display changes, which is the usual failure of remembered window positions.

alternatives.option: A normal SwiftUI window
alternatives.tradeoff: Standard behavior and less AppKit; it activates the application and changes the frontmost application, breaking delivery targeting.

alternatives.option: Menu bar popover only
alternatives.tradeoff: No extra window; anchored to the menu bar so it cannot sit near where the user is typing, and it dismisses on outside clicks.

alternatives.option: Promote the provisional transcript as the final result
alternatives.tradeoff: Feels faster; delivers text produced from partial context as final, the confusion the requirement asks to prevent.

decisions.consequences: Panel focus and level behavior is AppKit-managed with SwiftUI content and needs its own tests. Users see text change when the final transcript arrives, which is highlighted rather than silent. When the scheduler denies the provisional pass, the panel shows preview paused rather than a stalled transcript.
decisions.reconsider_when: The phase 2 measurement shows the provisional pass costs dropped buffers or final-transcript quality, in which case the preview degrades to waveform plus a voice-activity indicator.

decisions.title: Modes as versioned revisions with structured transformation contracts and a fail-closed validator
decisions.choice: Every mode, built-in or custom, carries a structured `TransformationContract` (allowed operations, `answersQuestions` flag, a content bound of recall threshold or citation requirement, and the list of languages its validator supports) alongside its free-form prompt. Revisions are content-addressed over prompt, formatting rules, contract, and model selections, and runs pin a revision id. Generated output is checked against the contract in the run's language: interrogatives present in the normalized transcript survive in order unless `answersQuestions` is declared; expansion ratio stays under the mode's limit; content-word recall exceeds the threshold; no span of eight or more tokens appears that is present in the context block and absent from the transcript; sentences with no content-word support in the input are flagged. On failure the run retries once with a stricter instruction, then falls back to the normalized transcript, marked as a validator fallback. When the run's language has no validator pack for the mode, the generation stage is skipped and the normalized transcript is used, unless the user sets a per-mode override that is off by default and recorded on the result.
decisions.rationale: Prompt wording cannot enforce that a dictated question stays a question, particularly when context contains instruction-shaped text, and delimiter framing influences a model without constraining it. Making permitted transformations a machine-checkable property turns the requirement into a gate with a defined failure path. Custom modes need a structured contract precisely because their prompts are free-form, so the contract is a required field rather than something inferred from prose. Failing closed on an unvalidatable language keeps the multilingual promise of D-017 from quietly bypassing the gate.

alternatives.option: Prompt instructions only, no validator
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplest and preserves whatever the model produces; the failure mode is a model answering a dictated question and the answer being pasted into a document.

alternatives.option: Infer permitted transformations from the custom prompt
alternatives.tradeoff: Nothing extra for the user to fill in; the inference is itself a language-model judgment with the failure mode it is meant to catch.

alternatives.option: Validate with a second model asked whether the output is faithful
alternatives.tradeoff: Catches semantic drift lexical checks miss; costs a second generation pass on the latency path and inherits the same failure mode.

alternatives.option: Deliver unvalidated output for unsupported languages
alternatives.tradeoff: No degradation for multilingual users; the contract stops being enforced exactly where the user cannot check it themselves.

decisions.consequences: The custom mode editor cannot save a mode without a contract, which is friction the editor must make quick with presets. Thresholds need tuning against the fidelity corpus, and bad thresholds show up as frequent visible fallbacks. Languages ship with packs one at a time, so multilingual rewriting is limited by pack coverage rather than by model coverage, and the panel says which. Lexical checks remain necessary conditions, which is why the adversarial corpus in verification is the ongoing check.
decisions.reconsider_when: Fallback rates stay high on correct outputs, the adversarial corpus finds a violation class that passes every check, or pack coverage becomes the binding limit on multilingual use.

decisions.title: Built-in mode set and their contracts
decisions.choice: Four read-only built-in modes, each with an explicit contract. Standard: punctuation, capitalization, optional disfluency removal, vocabulary substitution; no reordering, no summarizing, no answering. Email: Standard plus salutation and sign-off from a template, paragraph breaks, register adjustment, no new factual content, recall-bounded body. Note: adds list and heading structure, recall-bounded. Meeting notes: summarization permitted, bounded by a citation requirement where every bullet references a real segment range and uncited bullets are dropped. All four declare `answersQuestions: false`. English packs ship first; other languages fall back per D-012 until their packs exist.
decisions.rationale: The specification asks for ordinary dictation plus task-specific output with permitted transformations specified per mode. Meeting notes is the one mode where summarization is the point, so recall cannot be its guard and a citation requirement fits what it is allowed to do.

alternatives.option: One configurable mode with toggles
alternatives.tradeoff: Less to explain; the contract dissolves into a toggle matrix that is hard to validate against.
